docs.title: Breakouts Engine and the execution robot (Projects and Experience pages)
docs.text:
The Breakouts Engine is the quantitative research engine behind breakouts.trade. It implements a channel-breakout strategy as a single source of truth that research and execution share, so backtests and the live bot import the same strategy code through a parity bridge. A nightly scanner pipeline runs over a regenerable local market-data lake and serves chart data from object storage. The research code carries parity, look-ahead, survivorship and point-in-time test guards meant to keep results reproducible.

Evan also built an execution robot for an Interactive Brokers account that has traded real money. The engineering he points to is the safety work around it: systemd units, a kill switch, an order gate and loss rails, broker-versus-journal reconciliation on a fixed short interval, and a heartbeat that names the running commit. This page makes no claim about the robot's live trading performance.

The engine produced a survivorship-free backtest ledger and a holdout period that was run once. Its published figures are the accepted claims on the /verify page; every one of them is a backtest or test-count figure, not a live trading result. The repository is private.

docs.title: breakouts.trade, the study tool (Experience and Projects pages)
docs.text:
Evan founded breakouts.trade and is its sole engineer and the only contributor to its repositories. It is a browser drill app that teaches a breakout stock-trading strategy on real charts, plus a daily scanner that runs on the same strategy code. It shipped to real users who sign up, activate and run practice drills.

Engineering work on the app:
- Reviewed every API route handler and the middleware, found a credentials path that accepted a password as proof of Google identity (a pre-auth account-takeover flaw), then fixed it and re-verified the fix.
- Hand-wrote idempotent SQL migrations and row-level-security policies with no ORM.
- Gated every pull request on type-check, lint, tests and build.
- Replaced a stock-metadata cold path that fanned out storage reads and timed out on cold starts with one precomputed artifact, and added a test that proves the fan-out is gone.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, React, Python, PostgreSQL, Supabase, GitHub Actions. The repository is private; the live site is breakouts.trade.

docs.text: For UC Berkeley's Econ 143 (Econometrics: Advanced Methods), Evan ran a quantile-regression study of whether pre-breakout volume contraction predicts upper-tail returns on Qullamaggie-style momentum setups. He locked the hypothesis in a timestamped commit before the estimator ran, then reported the null as it came, with a bootstrap interval and a shuffled-label placebo. docs.title: LLM Energy Benchmark (Projects and Experience pages)
docs.text:
Evan initiated and built a measurement pipeline for the energy cost of LLM API usage. It ingests and cleans large conversation datasets, replays the extracted prompts against several hosted models, records power draw with CodeCarbon, and engineers many linguistic features per prompt.

Measurement scope: the CodeCarbon tracker runs on the local client during each remote API call, so it captures client-side power draw across the request window, not provider-side inference energy, which these APIs do not expose.

The result was null: no prompt characteristic predicted client-side energy. Request duration dominated the measurement, which is the expected behavior for a client-side tracker and explains the missing prompt-feature signal. The negative result runs against the project's original hypothesis, and he reports it as such. Code: github.com/evwillow/llm-energy-benchmark.

docs.title: Market Open Momentum (Projects page)
docs.text: A deterministic, rule-based strategy that trades early-morning momentum divergence between leveraged ETFs. It opens equal-dollar positions in UPRO and SPXU at the market open, closes the losing side once a spread threshold resolves within a short evaluation window, and exits the winner on a configurable schedule (same-day close or overnight hold). There is no model fitting, so results are reproducible run to run. The backtest engine models slippage and tracks pattern-day-trading limits. Code: github.com/evwillow/marketOpenMomentum.

docs.title: evwillow.com and this Ask page (Projects page and /ask)
docs.text:
evwillow.com is a Next.js App Router portfolio and blog. Posts are authored as local MDX or in Contentful and rendered through a shared pipeline, with JSON-LD structured data and a generated sitemap (github.com/evwillow/personalSite).

This Ask page answers questions about Evan's work only from an allowlisted set of sources: the site pages, his public GitHub READMEs and the accepted claims on /verify. Every answer cites its sources. A plain-code validator checks each answer after it is generated and blocks it if it states a number that does not match a cited accepted claim. The server route has a per-IP rate limit and a daily dollar cap; when the cap is reached the page pauses until the next day. Analytics record only a question category and a hash of the question, never its text.

docs.title: How I verify results (/verify page)
docs.text:
Every number Evan publishes about the trading research is meant to be re-derivable from a command, an input file and a commit. A number is published only after it clears four rungs in order. First, the claim, stated with its scope (which ledger, which years, how many trades). Second, the source command that produces the value, run at a recorded commit. Third, the sha256 hash of every input file the command read, so a changed input is detectable. Fourth, an independent rerun from a clean checkout by a separate process that must give the same value.

The /verify page lists the accepted numbers with commit and input hash, and keeps a retraction log of earlier values he withdrew after re-deriving them. The raw ledger is not published, so reproducing a value needs access from Evan; the commands, commits and hashes are in the site repository.

# Measuring Prompt Energy in LLMs

A comprehensive research toolkit for analyzing energy consumption patterns across different Large Language Models (LLMs). This project measures and compares the energy efficiency of various AI models when processing different types of prompts.

## Overview

This research project provides tools to:
- Download and process large conversation datasets
- Extract and clean prompts from conversations
- Measure energy consumption of different LLM models
- Perform feature engineering and exploratory analysis
- Conduct statistical analysis and generate insights

## Project Structure

**Step [n]: Analysis (Coming Soon)**

## Detailed Usage

### Data Collection (`[n]_data_collection.ipynb`)

This notebook downloads the LMSYS Chat [n]M dataset:

- **Source**: Hugging Face `lmsys/lmsys-chat-[n]m` dataset
- **Output**: `data/raw_conversations.jsonl` - Raw conversation data
- **Features**:
  - Streams data to avoid memory issues

**Key Configuration**:

This notebook extracts and cleans user prompts from conversation data:

- **Input**: `data/raw_conversations.jsonl` - Raw conversation data
- **Output**: `data/clean_prompts.jsonl` - Cleaned prompts with metadata
- **Features**:
  - Filters for English conversations only
  - Validates prompt quality (length, uniqueness, content)
  - Generates prompt statistics and visualizations

**Key Configuration**:

### Energy Measurement (`[n]_energy_measurement.ipynb`)

This notebook measures energy consumption across different LLM models:

- **Supported Models**: OpenAI GPT-[n]o-mini, Groq Llama-[n]-[n]b, Mistral Large
- **Metrics Tracked**:
  - Energy consumption (Wh)
  - Processing time and speed
  - Token usage and efficiency
  - Response quality metrics

**Key Features**:
- Incremental processing with resume capability
- Real-time progress tracking
- Automatic error handling and retry logic
- Batch result saving

### Feature Engineering (`[n]_feature_engineering.ipynb`)

This notebook creates comprehensive linguistic and semantic features from prompt text:

**Text Complexity Features:**
- `syntactic_tree_depth` - Maximum depth of syntactic parse tree
- `clause_count` - Number of clause markers and conjunctions
- `flesch_kincaid_grade` - Readability grade level
- `gunning_fog_index` - Text complexity index

**Lexical Features:**
- `avg_word_frequency` - Average frequency of words in English
- `lexical_diversity` - Diversity of vocabulary (sqrt normalization)
- `type_token_ratio` - Ratio of unique words to total words

**Semantic Features:**
- `named_entity_density` - Density of named entities (persons, places, organizations)
- `semantic_category_diversity` - Diversity of part-of-speech categories

**Sentiment Features:**
- `sentiment_polarity` - Overall sentiment score ([n] to [n])
- `sentiment_intensity` - Intensity of sentiment expression

**Information Content:**
- `information_density` - Ratio of content words to total words
- `avg_sentence_length_prompt` - Average words per sentence

**Topic Keyword Density ([n] categories):**
- `tech_ai_density` - Technology and AI-related keywords
- `business_finance_density` - Business and finance keywords
- `health_medical_density` - Health and medical keywords
- `education_learning_density` - Education and learning keywords
- `science_research_density` - Science and research keywords
- `social_relationships_density` - Social and relationship keywords
- `entertainment_culture_density` - Entertainment and culture keywords
- `travel_lifestyle_density` - Travel and lifestyle keywords

**Concept Density ([n] categories):**
- `abstract_thinking_density` - Abstract and philosophical concepts
- `problem_solving_density` - Problem-solving and analytical concepts
- `communication_density` - Communication and language concepts
- `emotional_psychological_density` - Emotional and psychological concepts
- `decision_making_density` - Decision-making and choice concepts

**Output**: `energy_features_dataset.jsonl` - Dataset with all engineered features

### Analysis Notebooks (Coming Soon)

- **Exploratory Data Analysis** (`[n]_exploratory_data_analysis.ipynb`): Visualize patterns and relationships
- **Statistical Analysis** (`[n]_statistical_analysis.ipynb`): Conduct hypothesis tests and statistical modeling

## Configuration Options

### Model Configuration

The energy measurement supports multiple models with different configurations:

### Data Processing Options

## Key Metrics Explained

- **Energy Consumption (Wh)**: Total energy used per request
- **Duration**: Total processing time in seconds
- **Time to First Token**: Latency before response starts
- **Tokens per Second**: Processing throughput

## Troubleshooting

# UPRO/SPXU Morning-Momentum Strategy

A deterministic, rule-based trading strategy that exploits early-morning momentum divergence between leveraged ETFs. The strategy enters simultaneous positions in UPRO ([n] bull) and SPXU ([n] bear) at market open, then closes the losing side after a [n]-minute evaluation window.

## Strategy Overview

### Core Mechanism

This is a **duel strategy** where two opposing leveraged ETFs compete for dominance in the first [n] minutes of trading. The strategy captures directional momentum while hedging initial market uncertainty.

**Daily Workflow:**

[n]. **Morning Cleanup ([n]:[n])** - Close any overnight positions from previous day
[n]. **PDT Gate Check** - Verify Pattern Day Trading limits allow new positions
[n]. **Duel Entry ([n]:[n])** - Buy equal dollar amounts of UPRO and SPXU
[n]. **Winner Detection ([n]:[n]-[n]:[n])** - Monitor [n]-minute window for [n] spread
[n]. **Close Loser** - Sell underperforming ETF when winner emerges
[n]. **Close Winner** - Exit remaining position at next day open OR same day close (configurable)

### Key Features

- **Deterministic execution** - No machine learning, fully rule-based
- **PDT-aware** - Tracks rolling [n]-day pattern day trade limits
- **Configurable exit modes** - Switch between overnight hold or same-day close
- **Backtested [n]-present** - Historical simulation with realistic slippage
- **SPX proxy simulation** - Uses SPX data to simulate UPRO/SPXU behavior ([n]/[n] leverage)

## Project Structure

## Configuration

All strategy parameters are centralized in `config.py`:

**Position Sizing:**
- `POSITION_SIZE_PCT` - Fraction of cash to allocate (default: [n])

**Winner Detection:**
- `SPREAD_THRESHOLD` - Minimum spread to declare winner (default: [n] = [n])
- Winner window is fixed at [n] minutes ([n]:[n]-[n]:[n])

**Exit Modes:**
- `EXIT_MODE = "next_open"` - Hold winner overnight, exit at next day [n]:[n] ([n] day trade)
- `EXIT_MODE = "same_close"` - Exit winner at [n]:[n] same day ([n] day trades)

**PDT Rules:**
- `USE_PDT_LIMITS` - Enable/disable PDT tracking (default: True)
- `PDT_THRESHOLD_EQUITY` - Equity level where PDT rules apply (default: $[n])
- `PDT_MAX_TRADES` - Max day trades in rolling [n] business days (default: [n])

**Trading Costs:**
- `SLIPPAGE_BPS` - Slippage per trade in basis points (default: [n] bps)

**Backtest Parameters:**
- `START_CAPITAL` - Starting equity for simulation (default: $[n])
- `START_YEAR` - Beginning year for backtest (default: [n])
- `UPRO_LEVERAGE` / `SPXU_LEVERAGE` - Leverage multipliers ([n] / [n])

## Installation

### Requirements

- Python [n]+
- Jupyter Notebook/Lab
- Internet connection for initial SPX data download

### Setup

## Usage

### [n]. Run Notebooks in Sequence

Execute notebooks in order to generate data and run backtest:

**Notebook Workflow:**

[n]. **[n]_environment.ipynb** - Load strategy configuration and verify setup
[n]. **[n]_feature_engineering.ipynb** - Download SPX data, simulate UPRO/SPXU, filter to regular hours
[n]. **[n]_model_training.ipynb** - Placeholder (strategy is rule-based, no training needed)
[n]. **[n]_backtest.ipynb** - Run complete backtest with equity curves and performance metrics
[n]. **[n]_diagnostics.ipynb** - Validate data quality, PDT logic, and determinism

### [n]. Initial Data Download

On first run, `[n]_feature_engineering.ipynb` will:
- Download SPX/USD [n]-minute data from HistData.com ([n]-present, parallel downloads)
- Save as year-based CSV files (`prices_2010.csv`, `prices_2011.csv`, etc.)
- Cache ZIP files in `data/histdata_cache/` for faster re-downloads
- Simulate UPRO/SPXU from SPX data using [n]/[n] leverage
- Filter to regular market hours ([n]:[n]-[n]:[n] ET)

**Note:** Initial download uses parallel workers for speed. Subsequent runs use cached files.

### [n]. Analyze Results

After running `[n]_backtest.ipynb`, review:
- **Equity curve** - Visual performance over time
- **Trade log** - Complete record of all entries/exits (saved to `data/trade_log.csv`)
- **Trade breakdown** - P&L by role (entry, cleanup, loser, winner)

### [n]. Validate Determinism

Run `[n]_diagnostics.ipynb` to verify:
- No NaN values or duplicate timestamps
- UPRO/SPXU data properly aligned
- Winner window timestamps exist for all trading days
- PDT tracker correctly enforces limits
- Backtest produces identical results on re-run (regression test)

## Data Management

### SPX Data Source

Historical SPX/USD data comes from HistData.com:
- Free [n]-minute OHLCV bars
- Available from [n] onwards (some years may have limited data)
- Saved as year-based CSV files to keep file sizes manageable
- Parallel downloads for faster initial setup

### Data Files (Excluded from Git)

Large data files are excluded via `.gitignore`:
- `data/prices_*.csv` - Year-based SPX price files (~[n]-[n] MB each)
- `data/upro_prices.csv` - Simulated UPRO prices
- `data/spxu_prices.csv` - Simulated SPXU prices
- `data/equity_curve.csv` - Backtest equity curve
- `data/trade_log.csv` - Trade history
- `data/histdata_cache/*.zip` - Cached downloads

**To regenerate:** Simply delete files and re-run notebooks.

## Performance Metrics

The backtest calculates:

- **Total Return** - Cumulative percentage gain/loss
- **Sharpe Ratio** - Risk-adjusted returns (annualized)
- **Max Drawdown** - Largest peak-to-trough decline
- **Win Rate** - Percentage of profitable bars

## Testing

### Automated Validation

Run `[n]_diagnostics.ipynb` to execute:
- Data quality checks (no NaNs, duplicates, alignment)
- Timestamp validation ([n]:[n]-[n]:[n] window exists)
- PDT tracker unit tests
- Determinism regression tests (identical results on re-run)

### Manual Testing

Test configuration changes by modifying `config.py` and re-running backtest:

## Export Notebooks to PDF

Generate PDF documentation of all notebooks:

PDFs are saved to `notebook_pdfs/` directory with execution results included.

## Architecture Notes

# EC143 Final Project

Pre-registered quantile-regression test of whether Qullamaggie-style volume contraction during a stock's consolidation base raises the upper tail of [n]-day forward returns more than it raises the median, after controlling for FF3+UMD factor returns, sector fixed effects, and year fixed effects.

**Deliverable:** [`writeup.ipynb`](writeup.ipynb) at the repo root. Open it and run all cells — every figure, table, and number regenerates from the four committed parquets in `data/`.

**Pre-registered hypothesis:** `writeup.ipynb` §[n] (locked [n]-[n]-[n], before any QR fits ran).

## Setup

Python ≥ [n] required.

## Data

Only four parquets are committed under `data/`, one per analysis-stage output:

- `m3_setups_with_residuals.parquet` — main analysis panel ([n] setup-rows × M1+M2+M3 columns)
- `m4_results.parquet` — OLS + QR coefficient table on the training window
- `m5_oos_results.parquet` — expanding-window walk-forward summary
- `m6_bootstrap.parquet` — stationary block bootstrap draws (real + placebo)

`data/raw/` is gitignored — it sources Polygon daily bars from a separate `breakoutStudyTool` pipeline and is not redistributable. Intermediate stage parquets, the FF3+UMD factor panel, the SPY cache, and the yfinance ticker-type cache are also omitted from the committed tree; they regenerate from upstream sources on a full pipeline re-run (M3/M2 download Ken French and SPY automatically; M1's yfinance ticker-type cache is repopulated by `src/_fetch_ticker_types.py` and `src/_fetch_ticker_adr_fields.py`).

## Reproduction

To verify only the writeup: open `writeup.ipynb` and `Run All`. It loads the four committed parquets and regenerates every output inline.

To re-run the full pipeline from scratch: execute the modules in order. Each writes its outputs to `data/` and emits a per-stage validation report to `reports/` as a side effect (`reports/` is gitignored).

[n]. `python src/m0_audit.py` — survivorship + bad-bar audit. Writes `data/m0_audit_summary.json`.
[n]. `python src/m1_universe.py` — Qullamaggie consolidation-breakout detector. Writes `data/m1_setups.parquet`.
[n]. `python src/m2_features.py` — per-setup features (vol contraction, ADR, RS-vs-SPY, sector). Writes `data/m2_setups_with_features.parquet` and (if absent) caches `data/spy_daily.parquet`.
[n]. `python src/m3_factors.py` — FF3+UMD factor panel + [n]-day-forward residualization on [n]–[n] training. Writes `data/ff3_umd_daily.parquet`, `data/m3_setups_with_residuals.parquet`.
[n]. `python src/m4_estimation.py` — OLS + QR(τ ∈ {[n], [n], [n], [n], [n]}) on training. Writes `data/m4_results.parquet`.
[n]. `python src/m5_walkforward.py` — expanding-window OOS sign-consistency check, [n]–[n]. Writes `data/m5_oos_results.parquet`.
[n]. `python src/m6_bootstrap.py` — stationary block bootstrap CI + placebo (~[n] min). Writes `data/m6_bootstrap.parquet`.

# Maze Solver

This script utilizes a recursive algorithm to navigate and solve mazes represented in a CSV file format. The maze solver finds the path from the start to the goal, visualizing the process in real-time.

![Maze Solver Visualization](selfSolvingMaze.gif)

## Features

- **Recursive Algorithm**: Uses a depth-first search approach to explore and solve mazes.
- **Real-Time Visualization**: Displays the maze and the path taken using colored symbols.
- **Maze Representation**: Reads mazes from a CSV file, where `[n]` represents an open cell, `[n]` represents walls, `A` is the starting point, and `B` is the goal.

## Technologies Used

- **Python [n]** for scripting
- **CSV** for maze input
- **OS** and **Sys** for terminal operations
- **Time** for controlling the animation speed

## Installation

[n]. Clone the repository:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/evanmaus/maze-solver.git
   cd maze-solver
